hero.headline: U.S. military carries out fourth strike on suspected drug boat in Pacific, killing 3
hero.body:
The U.S. military conducted another lethal strike against a vessel suspected of carrying drugs in the eastern Pacific Ocean, according to an announcement from U.S. Southern Command. Three people were killed in the attack, which represents the latest in a series of operations targeting vessels along known drug trafficking routes.

The military said intelligence confirmed the boat was transiting along established narco-trafficking corridors and was engaged in drug smuggling operations. The strike was carried out "at the direction of" Pete Hegseth, the defense secretary. U.S. Southern Command stated on social media that no American military forces were harmed during the operation.

The latest strike adds to a larger campaign of naval attacks on suspected drug smugglers. Since September, the Pentagon has disclosed at least 30 known naval strikes, resulting in a death toll of at least 107 people according to U.S. military figures. The operations represent an escalation in U.S. maritime interdiction efforts in the region.

President Donald Trump has publicly defended the attacks, claiming each drug shipment intercepted would have caused 25,000 American deaths. Over the weekend, Trump told supporters on a New York radio show that the U.S. had destroyed a facility in Venezuela where boats are loaded with drugs. He later told reporters that the strike involved "a major explosion in the dock area where they load the boats up with drugs."

Neither the White House nor the Pentagon has provided additional details about the Venezuelan strike or confirmed whether it actually occurred. Trump stated that after targeting individual boats, the military then struck "the implementation area, that's where they implement, and that is no longer around."

The military has not disclosed specific information about the suspected origin or destination of the drugs, the nationality of those killed, or whether any narcotics were actually recovered from the vessels. Details about the location of the latest strike remain limited.

The series of operations has raised questions about the scale and intensity of the campaign, particularly given the number of casualties in such a short timeframe. The military has not publicly disclosed the specific legal authority under which the attacks are being conducted or whether the targeted boats were armed.

The Pacific Ocean has long served as a major corridor for drug trafficking organizations attempting to move illegal substances between production areas and consumer markets. The U.S. has conducted maritime interdiction operations in international waters for years, though the lethal force campaign currently underway appears to represent a shift in tactics and scale compared to previous enforcement efforts.

cards.headline: Trump sends revised terms back to Iran in nuclear deal negotiations
cards.teaser: The president returned text of a potential Iran agreement with changes, according to reports.
cards.body:
President Trump submitted a revised draft of a potential Iran deal with tougher terms, according to multiple news outlets. The move signals that negotiations will continue for at least another week as both sides work toward a peace framework.

Trump canceled personal plans over the Memorial Day weekend to focus on the negotiations, heightening speculation about a possible deal. However, core issues in the talks remain unresolved, and Trump has not yet decided whether to extend the existing ceasefire with Iran.

cards.headline: Israel seizes Beaufort Castle in Lebanon as ground offensive expands
cards.body:
Israeli forces have captured Beaufort Castle, a 900-year-old medieval fortress in southern Lebanon, marking their deepest military incursion into the country in more than 26 years. The capture signals a significant advance against Hezbollah and represents a pivotal moment in the ongoing conflict.

The castle sits on a commanding hilltop that overlooks much of southern Lebanon, giving it considerable strategic importance. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz confirmed the seizure, with images showing Israeli and Golani Brigade flags flying over the fortress as fighting continued in surrounding areas. The Israeli Defence Forces stated they had "launched an operation in the Beaufort Ridge and Wadi al-Saluki area of southern Lebanon to dismantle Hezbollah infrastructure and expand its control of the area."

The military's advance has taken Israeli forces across the Litani River for the first time in decades. The IDF said troops seized positions from which Hezbollah had directed attacks and launched rockets into Israel. The operation comes amid stalled negotiations between the US and Iran, with observers suggesting Israeli officials want to inflict maximum damage on Hezbollah before any international agreement could limit their offensive.

The castle's capture holds profound symbolic weight for both nations. During Israel's previous occupation of southern Lebanon from 1982 to 2000, the fortress served as a military base and became a focal point of resistance. For Lebanese, it represents their struggle against occupation. For Israelis, it evokes memories of their lengthy military presence.

Israeli forces are now positioned to potentially encircle Nabatieh, an economic and cultural centre in southern Lebanon. Control of surrounding hills would provide tactical advantages over large areas of southern Lebanon and the western Bekaa valley. For many Lebanese, Nabatieh carries deep historical significance as a symbol of resistance and remains embedded in the political memory of the region.

The Israeli military has issued evacuation orders for residents south of the Zahrani river as operations expand. Forces have already moved past towns including Zawtar al-Sharqiyah and Mayfadoun and are approaching Choukine, where residents were ordered to evacuate on Saturday.

Lebanon's Prime Minister Nawaf Salam accused Israel of "pursuing a scorched-earth policy and collective punishment" through destruction of towns and forced displacement. He described the situation as a "dangerous" escalation and called for a swift ceasefire. However, he defended his government's engagement with Israel, noting that security talks held in Washington on Friday represented "the least costly path for our country."

The Lebanese health ministry reports Israeli attacks have killed more than 3,371 people since March 2, when Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the broader Middle East conflict. A ceasefire agreement officially began in April but has never been observed, with both sides accusing each other of violations. The conflict remains far from resolution, with neither side showing willingness to de-escalate.

cards.headline: Colombia holds presidential election that could reshape US relations
cards.teaser: Colombians vote in a presidential race following months of public disputes between current left-wing President Gustavo Petro and US President Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Colombians voted in the first round of their presidential election, held amid escalating tensions between outgoing President Gustavo Petro and US President Donald Trump. The election comes a decade after Colombia signed a historic peace agreement with the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc), marking a significant moment for a nation shaped by decades of armed conflict.

The race presented starkly different visions for Colombia's future. Voters chose between candidates aligned with Petro's leftist policies and pro-Trump candidates advocating right-wing approaches. The election served as a referendum on Petro's record and the direction of peace and security policies going forward.

cards.headline: Children detained in ICE facility under prison-like conditions, report says
cards.teaser: CBS News reports children are being held in conditions compared to criminal detention.
cards.body:
A lawsuit filed against Immigration and Customs Enforcement alleges severe violations at Camp East Montana, the largest immigration detention facility in the US, located in Texas. Legal organizations brought a class-action complaint on behalf of detainees currently held at the facility and those who will be held there in the future.

The complaint details numerous problems including inadequate medical and mental health care, inappropriate use of force, solitary confinement, unsanitary living conditions, disease outbreaks, and sexual harassment by guards. Plaintiffs also reported that food provided was spoiled and inadequate, characterizing the overall conditions as "dire" and violating human and constitutional rights.

cards.headline: Experimental pill extends survival for advanced pancreatic cancer patients
cards.teaser: Researchers reported new results for a treatment targeting one of the deadliest cancer types.
cards.body:
A daily pill called daraxonrasib has doubled survival time for patients with advanced pancreatic cancer, according to clinical trial results. Experts are calling it a "gamechanger" and one of the biggest breakthroughs in decades for treating this disease.

Pancreatic cancer remains one of the world's deadliest cancers, with few effective treatments currently available. More than half of patients are diagnosed only after the cancer has spread. The new medication offers hope for patients with advanced disease who have long lacked therapeutic options.

cards.headline: Wheat farmers face worst crop in decades, grocery prices expected to rise
cards.teaser: Wheat farmers are experiencing their worst crop yields in decades due to poor growing conditions, with effects expected to reach grocery stores soon.
cards.body:
Original Card Text

Wheat farmers are facing the worst crop in decades this year due to a combination of poor growing conditions. The challenging circumstances have created what farmers describe as a perfect storm affecting wheat production.

The reduced wheat harvest is expected to have ripple effects that consumers will notice at grocery stores. Prices for wheat-based products could increase as a result of the diminished crop yields.

---

Note: The additional source material provided (about a $250 note and US-Iran oil talks) is unrelated to the wheat crop story. Therefore, I'm returning the original card text unchanged, as instructed.

cards.headline: Five rescued from flooded Laos cave as search continues for two missing men
cards.teaser: Survivors are helping rescuers plan operations to locate the final two men trapped in a narrow, flooded cave system in Laos.
cards.body:
Five men have been rescued from a flooded cave in Laos, while two remain missing. Seven villagers entered the narrow tunnels on 20 May in search of gold before becoming trapped by flooding.

The freed survivors are now helping rescue teams plan the next steps in the operation to find the two missing men still in the cave's flooded passages.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones strike Russian oil infrastructure in overnight attacks
cards.teaser: Ukrainian drones hit a pipeline, refinery, and fuel depot across multiple locations in Russia during coordinated overnight strikes.
cards.body:
Ukraine launched drone attacks on Russian energy targets overnight, striking a pipeline, an oil refinery, and a fuel depot across multiple locations. The Saratov refinery in southwestern Russia caught fire following the attack.

In a separate operation, Ukrainian forces destroyed a Tu-142MR aircraft, marking a significant loss for Russia's Northern Fleet.

cards.headline: Retired Nigerian general and wife kidnapped in northwest region
cards.teaser: Major General Rabe Abubakar and his wife were abducted, highlighting ongoing security challenges in parts of Nigeria.
cards.body:
Major General Rabe Abubakar and his wife were abducted in Nigeria's northwest region by unidentified attackers. The incident draws attention to the serious security challenges affecting parts of the country.

The kidnapping is the latest in a pattern of abductions and armed violence that has plagued the northwest in recent years, highlighting ongoing threats to safety in the region.

cards.headline: US boat strikes in South America pass 200 deaths as coastal residents reconsider livelihoods
cards.teaser: Residents of coastal communities in Colombia and Ecuador say the airstrike campaign is forcing many to abandon ocean-based work.
cards.body:
Deaths from US military strikes in South American waters have exceeded 200 since last year. The US Southern Command has conducted multiple operations targeting vessels it says are engaged in drug trafficking along routes in the eastern Pacific.

The strikes are reshaping life in coastal communities across Colombia and Ecuador. Residents dependent on maritime work for income are abandoning ocean-based livelihoods due to the campaign, fundamentally altering the economic landscape of these regions.

cards.headline: Taiwan examines security risks posed by mainland Chinese spouses
cards.teaser: A criminal case involving a wife from China raises questions about protecting democracy while avoiding unfair targeting of Chinese migrants.
cards.body:
Taiwan is grappling with concerns about potential infiltration through mainland Chinese spouses. A criminal case involving one such wife has brought the issue into focus.

At the center of the debate is how Taiwan can safeguard its democratic system without unfairly targeting Chinese migrants. The case has prompted broader examination of security measures and their impact on the Chinese spouse community in Taiwan.

cards.teaser: Israeli forces seized the 12th-century Beaufort castle overlooking the border region.
cards.body:
Israel's military has seized Beaufort Castle, a 12th-century fortress situated on high ground between southern Lebanon and northern Israel. The capture is part of a broader military offensive that the Israeli military says extends south of the Zahrani river, with orders for civilians in that region to evacuate.

The strategic location of the castle, which overlooks both sides of the border, suggests Israel intends to maintain a prolonged military presence in the area as its operations in southern Lebanon continue to expand.

cards.teaser: CBS News reports children are being held in conditions compared to criminal detention.

Plaintiffs also reported that food provided was spoiled and inadequate, characterizing the overall conditions as "dire" and violating human and constitutional rights.

cards.headline: White House economic adviser tells Americans to consider overall price picture
cards.teaser: Kevin Hassett urged consumers to look beyond short-term price fluctuations.
cards.body:
Kevin Hassett, the White House economic director, urged Americans to look at the whole picture on prices rather than focusing on individual increases. He told consumers to smooth through ups and downs in pricing, according to Politico and other outlets.

The comments came amid ongoing concerns about gas prices and inflation. Hassett made the remarks during an appearance on Face the Nation. Reports indicated consumer confidence data showed continuing economic anxiety among Americans.

cards.headline: Chicago Bears stadium funding bill collapses before Illinois deadline
cards.teaser: Negotiations broke down one day before the state legislative session ends.
cards.body:
A stadium funding bill for the Chicago Bears fell apart one day before the Illinois legislative deadline. Lawmakers had been working on proposals that included property tax breaks and other financing mechanisms to help keep the team in the state.

The Illinois General Assembly unveiled a $55 billion budget plan as stadium talks returned to the starting point on the final day of the spring session. Legislators were scrambling to craft an alternate plan for the Bears' proposed stadium project after the initial bill failed to advance.

hero.headline: Passenger Tries to Break Into Cockpit on Chicago Flight, Forcing Emergency Landing
hero.body:
A United Airlines flight traveling from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted to Madison, Wisconsin, after a passenger made repeated attempts to enter the cockpit. The incident aboard flight 2005 prompted a hijacking alert and an emergency landing on Friday evening.

Crew members reported that the passenger tried to breach the cockpit multiple times during the flight. According to air traffic communications, a crew member told ground control: "I do not believe they ever cuffed him, but they were able to finally get control of him after multiple attempts to try to breach the cockpit. I believe at this point he is seated in a seat and flanked with law enforcement officers on either side."

The aircraft landed safely at Dane County Regional Airport in Madison, where local law enforcement detained the passenger. The FBI in Milwaukee was notified of the diversion and responded to the airport along with local police. An FBI spokesperson confirmed that "a subject was detained by the sheriff's office, and afterwards passengers resumed their flight."

The flight carried 147 passengers and six crew members. No injuries were reported during the incident. United Airlines issued a statement saying flight 2005 "landed safely in Madison to address a security concern with an unruly passenger."

After the passenger was removed and law enforcement secured the scene, the remaining passengers continued their journey to Minneapolis, landing early Saturday morning, according to flight tracking data.

The incident underscores the serious nature of cockpit security in modern aviation. Federal regulations strictly prohibit unauthorized access to aircraft cockpits, and attempts to breach cockpit doors carry significant criminal penalties. Since the September 11 terrorist attacks in 2001, hijackings have become extremely rare in the United States. The last major wave of aircraft hijackings occurred between 1968 and 1972, when more than 130 U.S. planes were hijacked. Many hijackers during that period demanded to be flown to Cuba.

Airlines maintain extensive training protocols for crew members to respond to security threats, and cockpit doors have been hardened specifically to prevent unauthorized entry. The crew's ability to manage the situation and maintain control of the aircraft demonstrates the effectiveness of these safety measures.

The diversion represented a significant disruption for the flight, though most passengers ultimately reached their destination. United Airlines expressed appreciation for the crew's handling of the security incident. The airline did not release additional details about the passenger's identity or potential motivations for the attempted breach. Authorities have not announced charges or provided further information about the investigation.

cards.headline: China Factory Activity Stalls as Demand Weakens
cards.teaser: Manufacturing activity in China remained flat in May as weakening demand and rising energy costs weighed on production.
cards.body:
China's factory activity showed no growth in May, according to manufacturing data released over the weekend. The stagnation signals continuing pressure on the world's second-largest economy as demand softens.

Energy costs contributed to the slowdown, limiting production capacity for manufacturers. The flat performance in May raises questions about the strength of China's economic recovery. Non-manufacturing activity showed slight improvement, rising to 50.1 in May.

cards.headline: Lung Cancer Drug Cuts Death Risk by 34% in Chinese Clinical Trial
cards.teaser: A late-stage trial in China found that the drug ivonescimab reduced the risk of death by 34% in patients with squamous cell lung cancer.
cards.body:
Ivonescimab, developed by Akeso and Summit, extended survival for lung cancer patients in a late-stage clinical trial conducted in China. The drug showed a 34% reduction in death risk compared to PD-1 inhibitors when used in combination with chemotherapy.

The trial results were presented at an international oncology gathering in Chicago. The drug targets squamous cell lung cancer, a common form of the disease. The findings add to growing attention on clinical trials emerging from China's expanding biotechnology sector.

cards.headline: China's Growing Biotechnology Industry Draws Attention at Oncology Conference
cards.teaser: Clinical trials from China gained prominence at an international oncology meeting in Chicago as the country's biotechnology sector expands.
cards.body:
China's biotechnology sector is gaining prominence in global pharmaceutical research, with clinical trial results presented at an international oncology conference in Chicago. The participation of Chinese pharmaceutical companies and research institutions at the event demonstrates the country's expanding influence in drug development.

The growth of China's biotechnology industry has prompted concerns among American observers about shifting global leadership in pharmaceutical research. The increasing number and quality of clinical trials originating from Chinese institutions reflects the sector's advancing capabilities.

cards.headline: United Flight Returns to Newark After Bluetooth Name Triggers Security Alert
cards.teaser: A United Airlines flight to Spain turned back mid-ocean after a Bluetooth device name sparked a security concern.
cards.body:
United Airlines flight UA236 from Newark to Palma de Mallorca turned back shortly after takeoff on Saturday night due to security concerns involving a Bluetooth device. The crew repeatedly asked passengers to disable their Bluetooth connections during the incident.

According to passengers on the flight, a Bluetooth speaker was broadcasting a name containing a four-letter word that raised alarms among crew members. The aircraft returned safely to Newark as a precaution.

cards.headline: Musk Explores Merging SpaceX and Tesla Despite Financial Concerns
cards.teaser: Elon Musk is considering combining SpaceX and Tesla into a single company, though analysts say the merged entity would be unprofitable initially.
cards.body:
Elon Musk has proposed merging SpaceX and Tesla into a combined entity valued at $3.4 trillion. The deal would unite the rocket manufacturer with the electric vehicle maker under one corporate umbrella.

Financial analysts have flagged a significant problem: the merged company would operate at a loss from its inception. Some investors also worry that combining the two businesses could negatively impact Tesla shareholders, raising questions about the merger's viability despite its enormous projected valuation.

cards.headline: Electric Air Taxi Makes Test Flight in New York City
cards.teaser: Aviation startup Joby demonstrated an all-electric aircraft in Manhattan, though the vehicles still require regulatory approval before public use.
cards.body:
Joby Aviation demonstrated its electric air taxi in Manhattan as part of efforts to develop aircraft that could replace helicopters for short urban trips. The company is collaborating with the Trump administration to advance the technology.

Before electric air taxis can carry passengers, they must undergo extensive testing and receive approval from federal regulators. Safety evaluations are required for all new aviation technology before commercial service can begin.

hero.headline: Meteor explodes over Massachusetts, causes sonic boom heard across Boston area
hero.body:
NASA confirmed that a meteor exploded over the northeastern United States on Saturday afternoon, producing a sonic boom that startled thousands of residents across the Boston area. The fireball streaked across the sky at around 2:06 pm ET and detonated north of Cape Cod Bay.

The explosion created powerful booms that were heard widely throughout the region. Residents reported the unexpected noise shook their houses, and several people captured footage of the bright fireball on camera. The event was visible enough to register clearly in satellite imagery, lighting up the sky in broad daylight.

The initial confusion about what caused the disturbance prompted widespread speculation among residents before NASA provided confirmation. Many people took to social media to report what they had experienced, describing the unexpected shaking and noise that startled the region.

NASA's analysis determined that the sonic boom resulted from the meteor exploding as it entered Earth's atmosphere. When space rocks travel at extremely high speeds through the atmosphere, friction and pressure cause them to heat up dramatically and often break apart. This fragmentation creates the characteristic booming sound that can be heard over large distances.

The agency indicated that fragments from the meteor may have fallen into the water near Cape Cod Bay. NASA has not provided specific details about the exact size of the meteor or precise locations where any debris might have landed.

This type of meteoric event happens periodically but draws particular attention when it occurs over populated areas. The Boston area incident gained widespread notice because of how far the boom was heard and the initial confusion about its source.

According to NASA's website, most space rocks smaller than a football field will break apart in Earth's atmosphere. Though rare, these objects can occasionally explode in the air, as happened in this case over Massachusetts.

Sonic booms from meteors occur when space rocks enter the atmosphere at hypersonic speeds. The extreme conditions cause the rocks to heat intensely and fragment, releasing the energy that produces the audible boom heard across wide areas.

NASA regularly tracks and analyzes meteoric events as part of its ongoing monitoring of near-Earth objects. The agency uses various detection methods, including satellite data and eyewitness reports, to identify and study meteors that enter Earth's atmosphere.

The confirmation from NASA provided clarity about the natural phenomenon that had startled residents across the Boston metropolitan area. The event demonstrated how visible and impactful meteor explosions can be when they occur near population centers, even when the objects themselves are relatively small.

cards.headline: Apple previews iOS 27 overhaul with updated Siri and AI features
cards.teaser: Apple is preparing to release iOS 27 with changes to Siri and artificial intelligence capabilities.
cards.body:
Apple plans to overhaul iOS 27 with updates to Siri and AI features, according to early information about the upcoming release. Bloomberg reported that the company is making changes to its virtual assistant and artificial intelligence systems.

The updates represent part of Apple's annual iOS revision cycle. WWDC 2026 is expected to showcase the new features, with media outlets describing this year's event as focused on refinements and improvements to existing systems.

cards.headline: Black founders see highest quarterly funding since 2022
cards.teaser: Black entrepreneurs raised the most quarterly venture capital funding in nearly four years, though access challenges remain.
cards.body:
Black founders reached their highest quarterly venture capital funding levels since 2022, according to Crunchbase data. This represents a notable shift after years of declining investment in Black-led startups.

Despite the funding uptick, significant obstacles persist. Gené Teare, head of research at Crunchbase, highlighted that Black founders continue to struggle with limited access to investor networks and early introductions—factors that disadvantage them in securing capital.

cards.headline: Enhanced Games held competition allowing performance-enhancing drugs
cards.teaser: A sporting event where most athletes used performance-enhancing drugs took place, backed by tech industry interest.
cards.body:
The Enhanced Games held a competition in which a majority of athletes used performance-enhancing drugs. The event represents a departure from traditional sports competitions that ban such substances.

The competition may signal a new business model that the tech industry is prepared to support, according to reporting on the event. The Enhanced Games positions itself as an alternative approach to athletic competition with different rules around drug use than conventional sports organizations.

cards.headline: Little Nightmares 2 Enhanced Edition releases for Nintendo Switch 2
cards.teaser: The enhanced version of Little Nightmares 2 is now available on Nintendo's newest console.
cards.body:
Little Nightmares 2 Enhanced Edition is now available on Nintendo Switch 2. The enhanced version brings the atmospheric puzzle-platformer to Nintendo's latest console with improvements over the original release.

The game is ready for purchase on the Switch 2 platform, offering players an updated experience of the haunting adventure.

cards.headline: Nest of endangered curlew bird discovered in conservation area
cards.teaser: A conservation trust documented a nest and eggs belonging to an endangered curlew species.
cards.body:
The Sliabh Beagh Curlew Conservation Trust has documented the discovery of a curlew nest containing eggs. Video footage of the bird was shared by the organization to highlight the finding.

Curlews are protected species, and discoveries like this are important for tracking population health and breeding success in conservation areas.

cards.headline: Rucking walking trend gains attention for fitness benefits
cards.teaser: A weighted walking exercise method is drawing interest as a fitness approach.
cards.body:
Rucking, a walking trend that involves carrying weight in a backpack, is gaining attention in fitness circles. HuffPost highlighted the practice as worth trying for exercise benefits.

The method combines cardiovascular exercise with strength training by adding resistance to regular walking. Proponents describe it as an accessible way to increase workout intensity.

hero.headline: Iga Swiatek knocked out of French Open in fourth round
hero.body:
Kostyuk Stuns Swiatek at French Open

Marta Kostyuk delivered a stunning upset victory over Iga Swiatek in the fourth round at Roland Garros, defeating the three-time defending champion 7-5, 6-1. The result marked a significant breakthrough for the 15th-seeded Ukrainian player and ended Swiatek's tournament run on her 25th birthday.

Swiatek, the world number 3, had been expected to contend for her fifth French Open title. The Polish player arrived at Roland Garros with renewed confidence following a strong start to the tournament under her new coach, Francisco Roig. However, she produced one of the most difficult performances of her career on Court Philippe-Chatrier, a venue that has traditionally been her fortress.

Kostyuk's victory was particularly impressive given her momentum heading into the match. The Ukrainian player arrived at the fourth round riding a 15-match winning streak and had not lost on clay this year after capturing titles in Rouen and Madrid. She also carried confidence from her previous encounters with Swiatek, having faced her in Cincinnati.

"I definitely have a different feeling going into this match, because I feel like last time that I played her in Cincinnati, I lost this match way before it even started, and I don't feel the same this time," Kostyuk said before the fourth-round clash.

Swiatek had initially been positioned in what appeared to be a challenging section of the draw. The tournament narrative after the draw ceremony suggested she could face her nemesis Jelena Ostapenko and potentially meet Elena Rybakina in the semifinals. However, both Ostapenko and Rybakina exited in the second round, appearing to clear Swiatek's path.

The loss removes a major champion from the women's draw. Swiatek had dominated the French Open in recent years, winning four titles in five years including three consecutive championships. Her departure represents another significant casualty in a tournament that has seen several high-ranked players eliminated.

Kostyuk's performance demonstrated her ability to compete with the sport's elite players on clay. Her breakthrough victory marks the biggest win of her tournament so far, and she now advances to the quarterfinals.

The defeat on her birthday proved particularly difficult for Swiatek, who acknowledged her struggles in post-match comments. For much of her career, the Polish player had found ways through challenging situations at Roland Garros regardless of circumstances or opponent strength. On this Sunday afternoon, however, that resilience was nowhere to be found as she suffered one of the most lopsided defeats of her tenure on the Paris clay.

cards.headline: Liverpool parts ways with manager Arne Slot
cards.teaser: Liverpool announced the departure of head coach Arne Slot and will hold talks with potential replacement Andoni Iraola.
cards.body:
Liverpool released an official statement confirming that manager Arne Slot has left the club. The team's captain Virgil van Dijk became the first player to publicly respond to the news of Slot's departure.

The club plans to hold discussions with Andoni Iraola as a potential successor and is seeking to make a swift appointment. Liverpool is moving quickly to fill the managerial position as the team addresses what were described as tactical problems under Slot's leadership.

cards.headline: Uruguay selects Manuel Ugarte for World Cup squad, leaves out Luis Suarez
cards.teaser: Uruguay named Manchester United midfielder Manuel Ugarte to its World Cup roster but did not include veteran striker Luis Suarez.
cards.body:
Uruguay's World Cup squad includes Manchester United midfielder Manuel Ugarte. The selection marks a significant opportunity for the player ahead of the tournament this summer.

Veteran striker Luis Suarez has been left out of the squad, marking a notable absence from Uruguay's roster as the team prepares for the World Cup campaign.

cards.headline: England head coach suggests US holidays for players before World Cup
cards.teaser: Thomas Tuchel wants England players to travel to the United States before the tournament to adapt to time zones and weather conditions.
cards.body:
England head coach Thomas Tuchel has advised his players to take holidays in the United States before the World Cup. The suggestion is designed to help the squad acclimate to American time zones and weather conditions ahead of their tournament campaign.

England's World Cup campaign kicks off on 17 June, and Tuchel believes early adaptation to US conditions will benefit the team's preparation and performance during the tournament.

cards.headline: Tyler Fletcher receives Scotland World Cup call after limited club playing time
cards.teaser: Manchester United player Tyler Fletcher earned a spot on Scotland's World Cup roster despite playing only 17 minutes for his club.
cards.body:
Tyler Fletcher has been selected for Scotland's World Cup squad despite playing just 17 minutes for Manchester United this season. The unexpected call represents a remarkable turnaround for the player, who had anticipated attending the tournament as a spectator.

Fletcher's inclusion demonstrates Scotland's confidence in his ability at international level. The selection offers him an opportunity to compete at the World Cup despite his limited club playing time.

cards.headline: Illinois stadium funding bill for Chicago Bears collapses before legislative deadline
cards.teaser: A proposed tax break bill to help fund a new Chicago Bears stadium failed as Illinois lawmakers entered the final day of their legislative session.
cards.body:
Illinois legislators could not reach agreement on a stadium funding bill for the Chicago Bears as the spring legislative session approached its deadline. A proposed property tax break measure failed to advance, sending lawmakers back to develop an alternative plan.

Lawmakers are working on the final day of the session to craft a new proposal that could help keep the Bears in Illinois. The state budget plan totaling $55 billion was introduced separately, but the stadium talks remain unresolved.

cards.headline: Sabalenka and Osaka to play first French Open women's night match since 2023
cards.teaser: Aryna Sabalenka will face Naomi Osaka in a fourth-round match scheduled for the evening time slot at Roland Garros.
cards.body:
Aryna Sabalenka will face Naomi Osaka in a fourth-round match at the French Open on Monday in a historic scheduling decision. This will be the first women's match to be played during the tournament's night-time slot since 2023, marking a notable shift in how the French Open organizes its women's competition.

The evening session matchup represents the tournament's renewed commitment to featuring women's tennis in prime-time scheduling.

hero.headline: Trump calls for cancellation of America's 250th birthday concert after artist withdrawals
hero.teaser: President Trump said the planned concert celebrating America's 250th birthday should be canceled after multiple artists withdrew from the event.
hero.body:
President Trump called for canceling the concert celebrating America's 250th birthday after several performers withdrew. Artists including Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels, and country singer Martina McBride dropped out, citing concerns that the event would become political.

Trump suggested replacing the concert with a Make America Great Again rally instead. He criticized the performers and indicated he might appear at an alternative 250th anniversary celebration on the National Mall.

cards.headline: Virginia Governor Spanberger faces opposition from Democrats over 31 vetoes
cards.teaser: Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger is drawing criticism from members of her own party after vetoing 31 bills passed by the Democratic-led state legislature.
cards.body:
Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger has vetoed 31 bills from the Democratic-led state legislature, drawing attacks from members of her own party. The governor considers her actions moderate, but many Democrats have turned against her.

Spanberger is being criticized from multiple directions for her veto decisions. The legislative session has highlighted tensions between the governor and Democratic lawmakers who control the Virginia General Assembly.

cards.headline: Senator Kim calls week of clashes outside New Jersey ICE facility among most difficult of his life
cards.teaser: Senator Andy Kim described the past week of confrontations between law enforcement and protesters at a federal immigration detention center as one of the most difficult periods he has experienced.
cards.body:
Senator Andy Kim described the past week as one of the most difficult of his life, following clashes between law enforcement and demonstrators at Delaney Hall, a federal immigration detention center in Newark, New Jersey.

The protests focused on conditions inside the facility. Kim met with demonstrators outside the center last weekend as they gathered to show solidarity with detained migrants.

cards.headline: World Food Program director requests increased U.S. food aid after USAID changes
cards.teaser: World Food Program Executive Director Cindy McCain pressed the Trump administration for additional food assistance, saying the organization needs help.
cards.body:
World Food Program Executive Director Cindy McCain has called on the Trump administration to increase food aid to her organization. McCain made the appeal during an interview with CBS News, emphasizing that the WFP needs additional support.

The request comes as the administration has made changes to the U.S. Agency for International Development, which impacts WFP operations globally. The World Food Program is the United Nations' humanitarian organization responsible for providing food assistance around the world.

cards.headline: Pence says Republicans lost their way, Democrats lost their minds after Paxton Senate win
cards.teaser: Former Vice President Mike Pence criticized both political parties, saying Republicans have lost their way while Democrats have lost their minds.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Mike Pence criticized both major political parties during an appearance on NBC's "Meet the Press." He said Republicans have "lost our way," while accusing Democrats of having "lost their minds."

Host Kristen Welker asked Pence about his position on the upcoming Texas Senate race, which follows Ken Paxton's victory as the Republican nominee.

cards.headline: Social Security retirement age changes affect 2026 retirees
cards.teaser: Changes to the Social Security retirement age this year could affect benefits for people who planned to retire in 2026.
cards.body:
The retirement age for Social Security changed this year, potentially affecting people who expected to retire in 2026. Retiring this year could have a significant impact on Social Security benefits depending on a person's specific age.

The change means some individuals who entered 2026 thinking they were ready to retire may need to reconsider their plans. The adjustment to the retirement age threshold affects how benefits are calculated for new retirees.

cards.headline: Wheat farmers face worst crop in decades, grocery prices expected to rise
cards.teaser: Wheat farmers are experiencing their worst crop yields in decades due to poor growing conditions, with effects expected to reach grocery stores soon.
cards.body:
Original Card Text

Wheat farmers are facing the worst crop in decades this year due to a combination of poor growing conditions. The challenging circumstances have created what farmers describe as a perfect storm affecting wheat production.

The reduced wheat harvest is expected to have ripple effects that consumers will notice at grocery stores. Prices for wheat-based products could increase as a result of the diminished crop yields.
